name: Quote & Ship Inside NetSuite
tag: Rate shop and book without leaving the Sales Order

problem.heading: Rating happens outside the ERP — so nobody does it.
problem.body: The order lives in NetSuite, but rates live in carrier portals and email threads. Reps bounce between tabs, paste rates into spreadsheets, and the freight cost your team quotes rarely matches the freight cost you pay.

quote.text: I need to go back and send emails to our carriers and compare those quotes, pick one… then do the documents we need to do in NetSuite, send the packing list, the BOL, all that.

benefit.heading: The FreightPOP tab lives on the NetSuite transaction.
bullets: Quote, rate shop and book on Quotes, Sales Orders and Item Fulfillments — inside NetSuite
AutoCalc rates the transaction automatically; dual rate shop compares contract and spot
Auto Select Best Option books the cheapest compliant rate with zero clicks
Accessorials supported on the transaction; services filter by subsidiary
Freight cost at the Quote stage — know your margin before you commit

demo.caption: A sales order rates itself inside NetSuite — AutoCalc plus Auto Select books the best option without opening another tab.

roi.statLabel: carrier portals opened to book a shipment
roi.proof: Rating, booking, documents and tracking all happen on the NetSuite record via the FreightPOP SuiteApp — built for NetSuite 2026.1 and updated continuously.

name: Order-to-Ship Sync
tag: Orders flow in, tracking and cost flow back — automatically

problem.heading: Every shipment gets keyed twice.
problem.body: The order is typed into NetSuite, re-typed into the shipping tool, then the tracking number and final cost get typed back by hand. Manual data entry and copy-paste between systems are the two most common pains NetSuite shippers bring to us.

quote.text: I would not need to manually check a checkbox or select a drop-down… in order for that to happen, right?
quote.who: — IT lead, NetSuite shipper (integration scoping call)

benefit.heading: A closed loop between NetSuite and your freight.
bullets: Sales Orders and Item Fulfillments import in real time — or search-and-import from the Quote/Ship page
Tracking number, carrier and actual cost write back to the fulfillment automatically
Latest tracking status visible directly on the NetSuite record
SPS Commerce EDI supported — transaction-level tracking, multiple fulfillments per order
Batch import handles high-volume days without babysitting

demo.caption: An order imports from NetSuite, books with the best carrier, and writes tracking + cost back to the fulfillment — no re-keying.

roi.statLabel: data entry eliminated on every shipment
roi.proof: Order data is entered once, in NetSuite. FreightPOP handles the round trip — the #1 and #2 pains NetSuite shippers report both disappear.

name: Product Catalog & AutoCalc
tag: Item dims and weights sync so rating is instant and accurate

problem.heading: Rating is only as good as your item data.
problem.body: Dimensions, weights and freight classes live in the item master — or in someone's memory. When they don't flow to rating, every quote is a guess and every reclass is a surcharge.

quote.text: We're trying to manually go through 9,000 part numbers to figure out what we need.

benefit.heading: The item master drives rating — automatically.
bullets: FreightPOP fields (dims, weight, freight class) on NetSuite items — including assembly items
AutoCalc configuration toggles sync from the item master; no double configuration
Auto-packaging logic builds shipments from catalog data
Update the item once in NetSuite — rating everywhere reflects it

demo.caption: A fulfillment rates itself from item-master dims and weights — no manual measuring, no guessed freight class.

roi.statLabel: SKUs rated straight from the item master
roi.proof: However large the catalog, item data syncs once and every quote uses it — accurate rates and fewer carrier reclass adjustments.

name: Order Change Management
tag: When NetSuite orders change, review and accept — nothing ships stale

problem.heading: The order changed after you planned the freight.
problem.body: Quantities move, addresses change, lines get added — after the shipment is already allocated. Without a control point, the wrong freight ships against the old version of the order.

quote.text: That has to be done so that we're not getting 2,000 orders weekly that are just going to sit there.
quote.who: — Operations program lead, NetSuite shipper (rollout planning call)

benefit.heading: Every ERP change gets a checkpoint.
bullets: Updates to an already-allocated order create a pending review copy — nothing is silently overwritten
Side-by-side comparison shows exactly which fields changed
Accept or reject in one click, with email notifications to the right people
Auto-accept rules clear low-risk changes without a human in the loop
High-volume order flow keeps moving — only real conflicts stop

demo.caption: A NetSuite order update arrives after allocation — FreightPOP shows the diff side-by-side and the planner accepts it in one click.

roi.statLabel: of order changes reviewed before they ship
roi.proof: Change management catches ERP updates against allocated shipments — the wrong-version shipment stops happening.

name: Consolidation & Optimization
tag: Combine NetSuite orders into fewer, cheaper shipments

problem.heading: Ten orders, ten shipments — one truck's worth of freight.
problem.body: Orders ship the moment they're ready, one at a time, because combining them by hand is slow and error-prone. The savings from consolidation are real, but nobody has time to hunt for them.

quote.text: We want to do it as quickly and efficiently as possible to have cost-savings realization — but not create so many manual processes that we stop shipping.

benefit.heading: Consolidation is a window, not a project.
bullets: Consolidation window inside NetSuite Native — select orders, rate them as one
Combine ERP-imported and manual orders in the same shipment
Zone-skipping support for parcel-heavy flows
Compare the consolidated rate against shipping individually — take the savings when they're real

demo.caption: Three NetSuite orders to the same region combine into one rated LTL shipment — the savings show before booking.

roi.statLabel: orders combined into a single rated shipment
roi.proof: Consolidation runs where the orders already live, so the cheapest way to ship is also the easiest.

name: Inbound PO Visibility
tag: Import purchase orders and track inbound freight to the dock

problem.heading: Inbound is a black hole until it hits the dock.
problem.body: Purchase orders go out, then silence. Receiving finds out a shipment arrived when the truck is in the yard, and production plans around inventory that may or may not be on a trailer somewhere.

quote.text: I find out a PO shipped when the truck shows up at the dock.

benefit.heading: Inbound freight, tracked like outbound.
bullets: Import purchase orders from NetSuite for inbound shipments
Book and track inbound freight in FreightPOP alongside outbound
Tracking updates export back to the NetSuite PO record
Receiving sees what's arriving and when — before the truck does
Feeds straight into WMS receiving when you run FreightPOP's warehouse layer

demo.caption: A NetSuite PO becomes a tracked inbound shipment — status updates flow back to the PO until it reaches the dock.

roi.proof: The PO record in NetSuite carries live tracking until delivery — receiving and planning finally see inbound the way customers see outbound.
